---
title: "Python interface"
---

This document describes the design of the Python functions forming the CLI and
the library layer, as well as tracking implementation status.

{{< include /docs/includes/_design-status.qmd >}}

## CLI

### {{< var done >}} `extract_metadata()`

`extract_metadata()` has two arguments: `parquet_path` and `output_path`. The
`parquet_path` argument is the path to a Parquet file in, e.g. the `staging/`
directory, and the `output_path` argument is the path to the Python script that
will have the `ResourceProperties()` dataclass filled in with the extracted
metadata.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-flow-extract-resource-metadata
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of objects and functions to extract a resource's
%%|   metadata from data.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   A flow diagram showing the steps to extract resource metadata from a
%%|   Parquet file.

flowchart
    parquet[/"Parquet data<br>[PARQUET-PATH]"/]
    read_parquet["read_parquet()"]
    output_opt[/"Output path<br>[--output]"/]
    output[/"Python script<br>[File]"/]
    data[("DataFrame<br>(Tidy)")]
    extract_metadata["extract_column_metadata()"]
    metadata[("ResourceProperties<br>(extracted)")]
    init_metadata["init_resource_metadata()"]

    parquet --> read_parquet
    read_parquet --> data
    data --> extract_metadata
    extract_metadata --> metadata -->|render<br>from<br>template| init_metadata
    output_opt --> write["write_file()"]
    init_metadata -->|string| write
    write --> output
```

### {{< var done >}} `init_metadata()`

`init_metadata()` has two arguments: `output_path` and `type`. The `output_path`
argument is the path to where the Python script will be created, which will
contain an empty `PackageProperties()` or `ResourceProperties()` dataclass. The
`type` argument is the type of metadata to create: `package` or `resource`.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-flow-init-metadata
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of objects and functions to compose the metadata
%%|   in a Python script.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   A flow diagram showing the steps to creating the Python file with the
%%|   empty metadata fields.

flowchart
    output_path[/"Output path<br>[output_path]"/]
    type[/"Type of metadata<br>[type]"/]
    template[/"Template<br>[File]"/]
    init_metadata["init_*_metadata()"]
    write_file("write_file()")
    output[/"Python script<br>[File]"/]

    type -->|package<br>or resource| init_metadata
    template --> init_metadata -->|string| write_file
    output_path --> write_file --> output
```

## Library

### {{< var planned >}} Metadata classes

These classes contain an explicit, structured set of official metadata defined
for a data package. The main purpose of these classes is to give programmatic
access to the structured metadata. That way the metadata can be generated from
writing Python code that, if it's possible, can processes some input source of
metadata into Sprout's metadata structure. The classes also make it easier to
get an overview or learn about what fields are part of the metadata in Sprout
(e.g. optional vs required fields) and what will be eventually generated into
the final data package.

See the help documentation with `help(Package())` for more details on the
metadata classes.

#### Class architecture

The class architecture follows the structure of the [TOML metadata
file](metadata-file.qmd) with two differences:

- Columns with different data types are represented by different classes, so
  that each class only defines the constraints applicable to its data type.

- `Package` does not have an `extend` attribute because extensions are resolved
  when the TOML metadata file is read.

The metadata classes exposed in the library interface are sketched out below.
The aim is to show the attributes and their types for each class, rather than
provide a full implementation plan. All classes are Pydantic models.

```python
class DataType(StrEnum):
    INTEGER = "integer"
    STRING = "string"
    BOOLEAN = "boolean"
    FLOAT = "float"
    DATE = "date"
    DATETIME = "datetime"
    TIME = "time"

class IntegerColumn:
    name: NonEmptyString
    title: NonEmptyString
    description: NonEmptyString
    required: bool = False
    unique: bool = False
    enum: Optional[list[int]] = None
    minimum: Optional[int] = None
    maximum: Optional[int] = None

class FloatColumn:
    name: NonEmptyString
    title: NonEmptyString
    description: NonEmptyString
    required: bool = False
    unique: bool = False
    minimum: Optional[float] = None
    maximum: Optional[float] = None

class BooleanColumn:
    name: NonEmptyString
    title: NonEmptyString
    description: NonEmptyString
    required: bool = False
    unique: bool = False

class StringColumn:
    name: NonEmptyString
    title: NonEmptyString
    description: NonEmptyString
    required: bool = False
    unique: bool = False
    enum: Optional[list[str]] = None
    pattern: Optional[str] = None
    min_length: Optional[int] = None
    max_length: Optional[int] = None

class DateColumn:
    name: NonEmptyString
    title: NonEmptyString
    description: NonEmptyString
    required: bool = False
    unique: bool = False
    # TODO: Consider if parsing is useful for checking constraints
    enum: Optional[list[str]] = None
    # In a specified format language
    format: Optional[str] = None
    minimum: Optional[str] = None
    maximum: Optional[str] = None

class DatetimeColumn:
    ...
    # same as in DateColumn

class TimeColumn:
    ...
    # same as in DateColumn

class ForeignKey:
    target_resource: NonEmptyString
    columns: NonEmptyList[NonEmptyString]

class Resource:
    name: NonEmptyString
    title: NonEmptyString
    description: NonEmptyString
    primary_key: NonEmptyList[NonEmptyString]
    foreign_keys: Optional[NonEmptyList[ForeignKey]] = None
    columns: NonEmptyList[any column type]

class Contributor:
    # TODO: decide which fields are required
    name: Optional[NonEmptyString] = None
    email: Optional[NonEmptyString] = None
    orcid: Optional[NonEmptyString] = None
    organisation: Optional[NonEmptyString] = None
    roles: Optional[NonEmptyList[NonEmptyString]] = None

class License:
    name: NonEmptyString
    file: Optional[Path] = None

class Package:
    name: NonEmptyString
    title: NonEmptyString
    description: NonEmptyString
    version: NonEmptyString = "0.1.0"
    homepage: Optional[NonEmptyString] = None
    repository: Optional[NonEmptyString] = None
    readme: Optional[Path] = None
    keywords: Optional[NonEmptyList[NonEmptyString]] = None
    observation_key: NonEmptyList[NonEmptyString]
    contributors: NonEmptyList[Contributor]
    licenses: NonEmptyList[License]
    resources: NonEmptyList[Resource]
```

#### Reading TOML files into metadata objects

When the TOML metadata file is read, resource, license, and contributor
extensions under `[extend]` are resolved into their corresponding metadata
classes as follows:

1. The metadata file at the given path is parsed into a Python dictionary.
2. The `extend` property, if it exists, is checked for correctness.
3. Each path in `extend.resources` is resolved relative to the directory
   containing the metadata file.
4. Each extension file is read into a `Resource` object.
5. These `Resource` objects are combined with the resources defined inline in
   the original metadata file.
6. Licenses and contributors are resolved in the same way.
7. A `Package` object is created from the Python dictionary, with the combined
   resources, licenses, and contributors.
